- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast highs when sentiment is positive or trending up.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment periods; raise forecast lows when sentiment is negative or trending down.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price increases — model tends to overreact; cap or smooth out such peaks.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model often lags — adjust forecast upward 1–2 periods ahead.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above or below recent 5–10 day average, pull toward historical mean unless sentiment overrides.
- Overshoot after volatility spikes: if price spikes >10% from recent high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate near-term momentum; reduce forecast slope for longer horizons unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
